evals.prompt: make a short clip of waves crashing on black sand at sunset, with seagull sounds
evals.expected_output: Calls gemini-media:generate_video with the default model (omni on the Gemini API, lite on Vertex AI), 720p or a 360p omni draft, 16:9, a prompt covering subject, action, camera and explicit audio cues (waves, seagulls). Then calls gemini-media:get_video with waitSeconds around 45 repeatedly until state is completed (no sleeping, no resubmitting), and reports the saved path/uri and cost. Is honest that it cannot watch the video.

evals.prompt: animate gemini-media://files/cat-on-roof.png - the cat should leap to the next roof as the camera follows
evals.expected_output: Uses image set to the given uri (image-to-video), aspectRatio matching the image (16:9 or 9:16), and a prompt describing motion and sound rather than re-describing the picture. Leaves personGeneration unset. Polls with get_video until completed and reports the file.

evals.prompt: I want a 4K, 8-second hero shot of our perfume bottle (bottle.png) rotating on a mirror, the highest quality you can do.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as expensive: calls gemini-media:estimate_cost (mediaType video, model standard, resolution 4k, durationSeconds 8, compare true) and tells the user the per-clip cost alongside the fast alternative before generating. Uses fast or standard (4k is not available on lite), durationSeconds 8, and either image=bottle.png or referenceImages=[bottle.png] (not both). On a [confirmation] error asks the user and retries with approvedCostUsd only after approval.

evals.prompt: extend the drone shot from job_7f3a2c by about 14 more seconds, flying over the ridge and down into the valley
evals.expected_output: Explains extension adds about 7 s per call, so plans two extend_video calls, each with a continuation prompt, polling each new jobId with get_video and using the second job's output (the combined video). Estimates the two extensions first. If the source job was made with lite or is older than 2 days, explains why extension fails and offers the last-frame-as-image alternative instead.

evals.prompt: Unattended run, nobody will be around to answer: produce a 9:16, 6-second teaser of a neon-lit city street in the rain for our app store listing.
evals.expected_output: Does not ask questions. Uses the default model (omni on the Gemini API, lite on Vertex AI) at 720p, or omni at 360p, aspectRatio 9:16, durationSeconds 6, a prompt with camera move and ambient sound. Stays under the confirmation threshold without setting approvedCostUsd, polls get_video until completed, and reports prompt, parameters, path, cost and what a fast/1080p version would cost.

evals.prompt: Use these three product photos as references and make the video start exactly on first.png, 4 seconds, on lite to keep it cheap.
evals.expected_output: Explains the conflicting constraints before spending: reference images require fast or standard, force 8 seconds and cannot be combined with a first frame. Proposes valid options (lite image-to-video from first.png at 4 s, or fast with referenceImages at 8 s) with estimate_cost figures, asks the user if present, or picks the cheap valid option and states the choice if autonomous.

evals.prompt: In the clip from job_0123456789abcdef01234567 the guy is holding a phone - can you make the phone disappear but keep everything else?
evals.expected_output: Calls gemini-media:edit_video with jobId set to the given job and a short prompt such as 'Make the phone invisible. Keep everything else the same.' (no model needed: edits use omni). States the estimated cost before or with the call. Polls gemini-media:get_video with the returned jobId until completed and reports the new file; does not regenerate the clip from scratch with generate_video.
